verses.text: Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian. And Moses led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.
And the angel of the LORD appeared to Moses in a flame of fire out of the middle of a bush. And Moses looked, and look, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed (burned up).
And Moses said: I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
And when the LORD saw that Moses turned aside to see, God called to Moses out of the middle of the bush, and said: Moses, Moses. And Moses said: Here am I.
And God said: Do not draw near here. Put off your shoes from off your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.
Moreover (also) God said: I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face, for Moses was afraid to look upon God.

And the LORD said: I have surely seen the affliction (suffering) of My people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of (because of) their taskmasters (slave bosses). For I know their sorrows.

And I am come down to deliver (rescue) them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good land and a large, to a land flowing with milk and honey. It is the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
Now therefore, look, the cry of the children of Israel is come to Me. And I have also seen the oppression (cruel treatment) with which the Egyptians oppress (treat cruelly) them.
Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, so that you may bring forth (out) My people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
And Moses said to God: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth (out) the children of Israel out of Egypt?

And God said: Certainly I will be with you. And this shall be a token (sign) to you, that I have sent you: When you have brought forth (out) the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God upon this mountain.

And Moses said to God: Look, when I come to the children of Israel, I shall say to them: The God of your fathers has sent me to you. And they shall say to me: What is His name? What shall I say to them?
And God said to Moses: I AM THAT I AM. And God said: This is what you shall say to the children of Israel: I AM has sent me to you.

And God said moreover (also) to Moses: This is what you shall say to the children of Israel: The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This is My name for ever, and this is My memorial (the way I am remembered) to all generations.

Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say to them: The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, appeared to me, saying: I have surely visited (looked after) you, and seen what is done to you in Egypt.

And I have said: I will bring you up out of the affliction (suffering) of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, to a land flowing with milk and honey.

And they shall hearken (listen) to your voice. And you shall come, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall say to him: The LORD God of the Hebrews has met with us. And now let us go, we beseech (beg) you, 3 days' journey into the wilderness (desert), so that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.
And I am sure that the king of Egypt will not let you go, no, not by a mighty hand.
And I will stretch out My hand, and smite (strike) Egypt with all My wonders which I will do in the middle of it. And after that Pharaoh will let you go.
And I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. And it shall come to pass that, when you go, you shall not go empty.

But every woman shall borrow (ask) of her neighbour, and of the woman who sojourns (stays) in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment (clothing). And you shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters. And you shall spoil (take the riches of) the Egyptians.

3.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed modern Bibles, e.g. "I Am Who I Am" in v14 and "ancestors" for fathers), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V14 keeps the KJV's I AM THAT I AM. V22 explains borrow as (ask), the meaning of the Hebrew word.

verses.text: Then the Lord said to Moses:
Tell the Israelites to go back to the town of Pi-Hahiroth and put up their tents there, between Migdol and the sea. They must camp near the sea and near Baal-Zephon.
Then Pharaoh will think that the Israelites do not know where to go. Pharaoh will say they are lost in the desert.

Pharaoh is stubborn, and Pharaoh will go after the Israelites and chase them. But I will defeat Pharaoh and his army. This will bring honor to me. Then the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord. The Israelites did what Moses told them.

When they told Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, that the Israelites had fled, Pharaoh and Pharaoh's officials said: We have made a mistake. We let the Israelites go and now they are not our slaves anymore.
So Pharaoh prepared his chariot and took his men with him.
Pharaoh took six hundred of his best men and all of his chariots. There was an officer in each chariot.
The Lord made Pharaoh, king of Egypt, stubborn. Pharaoh followed and chased the Israelites, but the Israelites were leaving with boldness.
The Egyptians with their war-chariots and the soldiers came near the Israelites, who were camping at the sea at PiHahiroth near BaalZephon.
When the Israelites saw Pharaoh and his army coming toward them, they were very afraid and cried to the Lord for help.
They said to Moses: Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us to the desert to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?

We told you this would happen! In Egypt we said, Please do not bother us. Let us stay and serve the Egyptians. It would have been better for us to stay and be slaves than to come out here and die in the desert.
But Moses answered the children of Israel: Do not be afraid! Do not run away! Stand where you are and watch the Lord save you today. You will never see these Egyptians again.
You will not have to do anything but stay calm. The Lord will do the fighting for you.
Then the Lord said to Moses, Why are you still crying to me? Tell the Israelites to start moving.
You must lift up your staff and hold it out over the sea. The water will separate and there will be dry ground for the Israelites to walk on.
I will make the Egyptians stubborn and they will go after you. I will show that I am God who can do what I want to do with Pharaoh and his army and his war-chariots and all his men.
Then Egypt will know that I am the Lord. They will honor me when I defeat Pharaoh and his horse soldiers and chariots.

Then the angel of God moved to the back of the people. (The angel was usually in front of the people, leading them.) So the tall cloud moved from in front of the people and went to the back of the people.

In this way the cloud stood between the Egyptians and the Israelites. There was light for the Israelites. But there was darkness for the Egyptians. So the Egyptians did not come any closer to the Israelites that night.
Moses raised his hand over the Red Sea, and the Lord caused a strong wind to blow from the east. The wind blew all night long. The sea split, and the wind made the ground dry.
The Israelites went through the sea on dry land. The water was like a wall on their right and on their left.
Then all of Pharaoh's chariots and horse soldiers followed them into the sea.
Early that morning the Lord looked down from the tall cloud and column of fire at the Egyptian army. Then the Lord threw the Egyptian army into a panic.
The wheels of the chariots became stuck. It was very hard to control the chariots. The Egyptians shouted, Let's get out of here! The Lord is fighting against us. He is fighting for the Israelites.
Then the Lord told Moses, Raise your hand over the sea to make the water fall and cover the Egyptian chariots and horse soldiers.

Then Moses put up his hand over the sea and the water of the sea flowed back to where it had been before. The Egyptians wanted to run away but the flood of water went over the Egyptians, and that is how God drowned the Egyptians in the sea.
The water returned to its normal level and covered the chariots and horse soldiers. Pharaoh's army had been chasing the Israelites, but that army was destroyed. None of them survived!
But the Israelites crossed the sea on dry land. The water was like a wall on their right and on their left.
So that day the Lord saved the Israelites from the Egyptians. Later, the Israelites saw the dead bodies of the Egyptians on the shore of the Red Sea.
The Israelites saw the great power of the Lord when he defeated the Egyptians. So, the people feared and respected the Lord, and they began to trust the Lord and his servant Moses.

14.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: And the LORD spoke to Moses: Go to Pharaoh, and say to him: This is what the LORD says: Let My people go, so that they may serve Me.
And if you refuse to let them go, look, I will smite (strike) all your borders (land) with frogs.

And the river shall bring forth (out) frogs abundantly (in great numbers). The frogs shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber (bedroom), and upon your bed, and into the house of your servants, and upon your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneadingtroughs (bread bowls).
And the frogs shall come up both on you, and upon your people, and upon all your servants.

And the LORD spoke to Moses: Say to Aaron: Stretch forth (out) your hand with your rod (staff) over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.
And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt. And the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
And the magicians did so with their enchantments (secret magic), and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.

Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said: Intreat (pray to) the LORD, that He may take away the frogs from me, and from my people. And I will let the people go, so that they may do sacrifice to the LORD.

And Moses said to Pharaoh: Glory over me (you choose the time). When shall I intreat (pray) for you, and for your servants, and for your people, to destroy the frogs from you and your houses, so that they may remain in the river only?
And Pharaoh said: To morrow (tomorrow). And Moses said: Be it according to your word, so that you may know that there is none like the LORD our God.
And the frogs shall depart (go away) from you, and from your houses, and from your servants, and from your people. They shall remain in the river only.
And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. And Moses cried to the LORD because of the frogs which the LORD had brought against Pharaoh.
And the LORD did according to the word of Moses. And the frogs died out of the houses, out of the villages, and out of the fields.
And they gathered the frogs together upon heaps (in piles). And the land stank.
But when Pharaoh saw that there was respite (a break), he hardened his heart (made himself stubborn), and hearkened (listened) not to them, as the LORD had said.
And the LORD said to Moses: Say to Aaron: Stretch out your rod (staff), and smite (strike) the dust of the land, so that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

And they did so. For Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod (staff), and smote (struck) the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast (animal). All the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
And the magicians did so with their enchantments (secret magic) to bring forth (out) lice, but they could not. So there were lice upon man, and upon beast (animal).
Then the magicians said to Pharaoh: This is the finger of God (the power of God). And Pharaoh's heart was hardened (stubborn), and he hearkened (listened) not to them, as the LORD had said.

And the LORD said to Moses: Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh. Lo (look), he comes forth (out) to the water. And say to him: This is what the LORD says: Let My people go, so that they may serve Me.

Else (otherwise), if you will not let My people go, look, I will send swarms of flies upon you, and upon your servants, and upon your people, and into your houses. And the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies, and also the ground on which they are.

And I will sever (set apart) in that day the land of Goshen, in which My people dwell (live), so that no swarms of flies shall be there. This is so that you may know that I am the LORD in the middle of the earth.
And I will put a division (difference) between My people and your people. To morrow (tomorrow) this sign shall be.

And the LORD did so. And there came a grievous (very heavy) swarm of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants' houses, and into all the land of Egypt. The land was corrupted (ruined) by reason of (because of) the swarm of flies.
And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said: Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.

And Moses said: It is not meet (right) to do so. For we shall sacrifice the abomination (a thing hated) of the Egyptians to the LORD our God. Lo (look), shall we sacrifice the abomination (a thing hated) of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us?
We will go 3 days' journey into the wilderness (desert), and sacrifice to the LORD our God, as He shall command us.
And Pharaoh said: I will let you go, so that you may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness (desert). Only you shall not go very far away. Intreat (pray) for me.

And Moses said: Look, I go out from you, and I will intreat (pray to) the LORD that the swarms of flies may depart (go away) from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, to morrow (tomorrow). But let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully (lie) any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to the LORD.
And Moses went out from Pharaoh, and intreated (prayed to) the LORD.
And the LORD did according to the word of Moses. And the LORD removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. There remained not one.
And Pharaoh hardened his heart (made himself stubborn) at this time also. Neither would he let the people go.

8.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that added things the KJV does not say, e.g. rotting frogs shoveled into piles in v14 and Egyptians worshipping cattle in v26, and changed lice to gnats), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V16-18 keep the KJV's lice. V26 keeps the KJV's abomination of the Egyptians.
